about: The front door: places and curiosities pinned on Ortelius's map of Tartary (M047). xy is in full-resolution pixels of the Library of Congress image. Only readings marked sure in the search notes are kept. The Latin is as read from the sheet and may be partial.

pins.on_map: Volga, et Edel, ol: Rha fl.
Mar de Bachu, olim Mare Caspium, et Hyrcanum.
Cambalu Cataie metropolis, habet 28. mill: in circuitu.

sights.title: The Duke of Muscovy's tent
sights.what: The borders of the Duke of Muscovy.
sights.latin: DVCIS MOSCOVIAE CONFINIA.

sights.title: The Great Khan's camp
sights.what: The Great Khan (which in the language of the Tartars means emperor), the greatest prince of Asia.
sights.latin: Magnus Cham, (quod lingua Tartarorum Imperatorem sonat) maximus Asie princeps.

sights.title: What the map claims to show
sights.what: This map contains all Tartary, together with the remaining part of eastern Asia as far as the Eastern Ocean, subject to the Great Khan; his empire is bounded by the river Ob, Lake Kataia, the river Volga, the Caspian Sea, the river Chesel, Mount Uson, the region of Tibet, the river Caromoran, and the ocean.
sights.latin: Continet hec tabula omnem Tartariam, cum reliqua Asie Orientalioris usque Oceanum Eoum parte, Magno Chamo obediente: Cuius imperium Obij fl: Kataia lacu; Volga fl: Mari Caspio, Chesel flu: Usonte monte, Thebet regione, Caromoram fluuio, et Oceano terminatur.

sights.title: The ten lost tribes
sights.what: Arsareth. Here the ten tribes withdrew and substituted [the name] Totars or Tartars for [that of] Scythia. Hence they were called Gauthae or Gauthay there, from upholding the supreme glory of God, and from this [comes] Cathay, a most renowned kingdom.
sights.latin: ARSARETH. Hic 10 Tribus secessere, et Totatorum sive Tartarorum loco Scythice substituerunt. Vnde Gauthae seu Gauthay a summa Dei gloria asserenda ibi dicti sunt, et hinc Cathay clarissimum Regnum.
sights.note: The middle clause is grammatically compressed; bracketed words supply an implied name. The reference above it is 4 Esdras, chapter 13.

sights.title: A horde named for a tribe of Israel
sights.what: The horde of the Nephthalites. The Nephthalites are named after Naphtali, one of the ten tribes of Israel; and after the Danites, who in their northern chastisement were called Danmarchi, they are placed second among the Hudaei or Jews, on account of the right of Rachel’s Bilhah. In the year of salvation 476 they were victorious against Perosa. Others incorrectly call them Euthalites.
sights.latin: Nepthalitarum horda. Nepthalite ab una 10. Tribuum Israelis nomine Neptali dicti sunt, et post Danitas qui in castigatione Aquilonari Danmarchi dicti sunt, ob Rachelis Balhah ius, secundo in loco Hudorum sive Iehudeorum sunt positi, et 476. salutis anno contra Perosa victores fuere, Euthalitas male vocant ceteri.
sights.note: The clause about Rachel’s Bilhah and the order of the tribes is obscure; this is a close, tentative rendering.

sights.title: The king of Tabor
sights.what: Tabor or Tybur, or the central region of the Totars, where, although they lost the sacred books long ago, they are nevertheless united under one king. In 1540 he came as far as France to King Francis, the first of that name, and afterwards, by Charles V, at Mantua, paid the penalty for his unbelief by fire; for he was secretly urging Christian princes to Judaism, concerning which he had spoken to Charles V.
sights.latin: Tabor seu Tybur, umbilicariave Totarorum regio, ubi licet olim libros sacros perdidissent, sunt tamen uniti sub uno rege, qui 1540. in Galliam usque ad regem Franciscum id nominis primum venit, et postea a Carolo V. Mantue igne sue infidelitatis poenas luit: quia secrete solicitabat Christianos principes ad Iudaismum, de qua re Carolum V. alloquutus erat.

sights.title: Prester John's kingdom
sights.what: Argon. There was formerly in Asia a kingdom of Christians under the name of Prester John, established there by Saint Thomas so that it might correspond with the Roman Church, obedient to Rome through Prester John the African. And before it was conquered by the Gothani, they were called Crive Romove.
sights.latin: ARGON. Christianorum olim regnum nomine Presbiteri Ioannis in Asia erat, a D. Thoma ibi institutum, ut Romane corresponderet ecclesie, per Presbiterum Ioannem Africanum Rome obediens. Et antequam a Gothanis vinceretur Crive Romove nuncupabantur.

sights.title: Printing, a thousand years early
sights.what: Tangut. Here they possessed the art of printing a thousand years ago, as they say.
sights.latin: TANGVT. Hic artem imprimendi ante mille, ut ferunt, annos habuerunt.

sights.title: The Strait of Anian
sights.what: The Strait of Anian.
sights.latin: STRETTO DI ANIAN

sights.title: Japan, attacked in vain
sights.what: The island of Japan, called Zipangri by Marco Polo of Venice, formerly Chryse, once attacked in war by the Great Khan, but in vain.
sights.latin: Iapan insula, a M. Paulo Veneto Zipangri dicta, olim Chryse, a Magno Cham olim bello petita sed frustra.

sights.title: America, across the strait
sights.what: Part of America, or the New World.
sights.latin: AMERICAE VEL NOVI ORBIS PARS

sights.title: The map’s title
sights.what: Map of Tartary, or of the kingdom of the Great Khan.
sights.latin: Tartariae sive Magni Chami Regni typus.

sights.title: The Scythian Ocean
sights.what: The Scythian Ocean is fresh, according to Pliny, who says that there are many islands in it, as does Marco Polo of Venice; but neither gives their position or number.
sights.latin: Oceanus Scythicus dulcis est Plinio auctore, qui multas in eo insulas esse dicit, ut etiam M. Paul: Venetus: sed neuter neque situm neque numerum tradit.

sights.title: Tartary, Sarmatia, and Scythia
sights.what: Tartary, which comprises Asian Sarmatia and both Scythias of the ancients.
sights.latin: Tartaria, quae Sarmatiam Asiaticam, et utramque Scythiam veterum comprehendit.

sights.title: Turkestan and the ten tribes
sights.what: The region of Turkestan, from which the allies of the ten tribes on this side of the mountains were summoned by the Persians 900 years ago against the arms of Muhammad the Ishmaelite.
sights.latin: Turchestan Regio unde cismontani 10. Tribuum socij ante 900 annos sunt accersiti a Persis contra Ismaelitae Mahumedis arma.

sights.title: Aromatic reeds
sights.what: Here there is an abundant growth of aromatic reed.
sights.latin: Hic magnus proventus calami aromatici.

sights.title: Ruby deposits
sights.what: Here ruby gemstones are found.
sights.latin: Hic Rubini gemmae reperiuntur.

sights.title: The burial mountain of the emperors
sights.what: Mount Altai, where all the emperors of Tartary are buried, appears to be described by Hayton the Armenian under the name Belgian.
sights.latin: Mons Althay, ubi omnes Tartariae imperatores sepeliuntur, ab Haytone Armeno sub nomine Belgian describi videtur.

sights.title: The Danes or Danites
sights.what: The horde of the Danes or Danites: casting down, descent, or expulsion.
sights.latin: Danorum sive Danitarum horda 1. deiectio sive descensio aut expulsio.

sights.title: Marco Polo’s falcon island
sights.what: The island of falcons, according to Marco Polo of Venice.
sights.latin: Insula falconum, M. Pauli Veneti.

sights.title: Cambalu’s circumference
sights.what: Cambalu, the chief city of Cathay, has a circumference of 28 miles.
sights.latin: Cambalu Cataiae metropolis, habet 28. mill: in circuitu.

sights.title: Stones burned instead of wood
sights.what: From these mountains stones are dug out which they use for the fire in place of wood.
sights.latin: His montibus eruuntur lapides, quibus utuntur ad focum loco lignorum.

sights.title: Quinsai, the city of heaven
sights.what: Quinsai, that is, the city of heaven.
sights.latin: Quinsai id est civitas celi.

sights.title: Rhubarb in the mountains
sights.what: Rhubarb grows in these mountains.
sights.latin: His montibus Rhabarbarum provenit.

sights.title: A marble bridge
sights.what: A marble bridge of 300 paces.
sights.latin: Pons marmoreus 300. pass:

sights.title: Meaco, Japan’s chief city
sights.what: Meaco, the chief city of the island.
sights.latin: Meaco insulae civitas primaria.

sights.title: Samarkand, seat of Tamerlane
sights.what: Samarkand, formerly the seat of the great Tamerlane.
sights.latin: Samarchand. magni Tamber: quondam sedes.

sights.title: Bargu’s marshland
sights.what: Bargu, a marshy region.
sights.latin: Bargu regio palustris.

sights.title: Cape Tabin in Pliny
sights.what: Cape Tabin, according to Pliny.
sights.latin: Tabin Prom: Plin.

sights.title: The printing privilege
sights.what: With privilege.
sights.latin: Cum Privilegio.

translation_audit.method: Attempted direct English translations of the inscriptions, checked against the full-resolution Library of Congress sheet. Abbreviations are expanded where possible. Formerly truncated Nephthalite, Tabor and Argon passages are now supplied in full. Brackets mark supplied words; uncertain readings are explained separately.
